row_label: Police Personnel killed on duty 14.1.1 The State, UT & City-wise information relating to Police Personnel Killed or injured on duty under various operations and accidents is provided in Table-83, while the rank-wise casualties or injuries sustained by these personnel is given in Table-84. 14.1.2 A remarkable decrease is noticed in the casualties of Police Personnel killed on duty during the last 5 years. 516 Civil police (including District Armed Police) personnel of various States & UTs sacrificed their lives while performing their duties, during the year (1995). Of the 516 Civil Police personnel killed, 505 belonged to the 25 Indian States and 11 to the 7 Union Territories.

columns.name: 14.1.3 While 65.1 per cent of the casualties were caused due to ‘Accidents’, ‘By Other Criminals’ accounted for 21.0 per cent, ‘Anti-Dacoity’ Operations and ‘Border duties’ 4.8 per cent and the ‘Riotous mobs’ 4.3 per cent. | 14.1.4 Punjab suffered the highest casualties (75) followed by Uttar Pradesh (71) and Maharashtra (47). The N.C.T. of Delhi recorded 9 deaths out of a total of 11 reported from the 7 Union Territories. It was a matter of consolidation for the States of Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Mizoram and Sikkim and the Union Territories of Chandigarh, D&N Haveli, Daman & Diu, Lakshadweep and Pondicherry, as in these centres no casualty was reported during the year. | 14.1.4 Punjab suffered the highest casualties (75) followed by Uttar Pradesh (71) and Maharashtra (47).
